title: 1、INT. LIGHTHOUSE - NIGHT.
content:
FADE IN:

INT. LIGHTHOUSE WATCH ROOM - NIGHT

A powerful beam rotates in the lantern room above. Below, in the watch room, MARCUS CALLOWAY (50s, weathered face, salt-and-pepper beard) moves between instrument panels. Each step reveals a pronounced limp -- his RIGHT LEG drags with a soft scrape while his left lands firmly.

Marcus wears THICK-FRAMED READING GLASSES perched at the end of his nose. He carries a BLUE CERAMIC MUG of steaming tea. He sets the mug on the corner of a worn wooden desk and opens a logbook, running his finger along the day's entries.

MARCUS
(murmuring)
Wind speed up two knots. Visibility holding at fourteen miles.

Below the desk, a BLACK LABRADOR -- ANCHOR -- raises his broad head from a sleeping mat and thumps his tail against the stone floor.

MARCUS (CONT'D)
(to the dog)
You smell it already, don't you, Anchor. Good boy.

Marcus limps back to the window, his right leg stiff and dragging, and adjusts the rotation mechanism with practiced hands. He resettles in his chair, lifts the blue mug, sips his tea, and watches the storm building on the horizon.

FADE TO BLACK.

title: 2、EXT. COASTAL ROAD / EXT. LIGHTHOUSE ENTRANCE - DAY.
content:
EXT. COASTAL ROAD - DAY

A RED JEEP rounds the final curve of a winding coastal highway. The ocean drops away to the left. Ahead, the lighthouse rises from a rocky promontory.

INT. RED JEEP - CONTINUOUS

ELENA VOSS (30s, sharp eyes, practical jacket) grips the steering wheel. On the passenger seat: a GREEN SPIRAL NOTEBOOK, its cover marked ELENA VOSS -- COASTAL HERALD. She glances at it.

ELENA
(muttering)
Calloway. End of the road.

She turns down the gravel track.

EXT. LIGHTHOUSE ENTRANCE - CONTINUOUS

Elena parks beside a weathered outbuilding and climbs out, GREEN SPIRAL NOTEBOOK tucked under her arm. MARCUS appears in the doorway, ANCHOR at his side.

MARCUS
You the journalist?

ELENA
Elena Voss. Coastal Herald. You spoke to my editor -- Claire Munroe?

MARCUS
She said you were thorough.

ELENA
She says what opens the door.

A pause. Marcus almost smiles.

MARCUS
Come in then. Storm's already in the air.

title: 3、INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S QUARTERS - DAY.
content:
INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S QUARTERS - DAY

A spare, lived-in room. Maritime charts and nets hang on the walls. Anchor trots to his corner beneath a wooden table.

Marcus sets a kettle on and places on the table a large BROWN LEATHER-BOUND LOGBOOK, its spine worn smooth from decades of handling.

MARCUS
Every keeper back to the first. Wind. Tide. Vessels. Distress calls.

Elena opens it with care. The handwriting changes across generations but the format is the same. She makes notes in her green spiral notebook.

ELENA
These gaps in 1974 -- what happened?

MARCUS
Before my time.

Elena notices a framed photograph on the shelf: Marcus younger, beside a woman with dark hair.

ELENA
Your wife?

MARCUS
(quietly)
Margaret. She passed three years ago. A stroke. Quick, at least.

ELENA
I'm sorry.

Anchor rests his black head on Elena's knee. She scratches behind his ear.

ELENA (CONT'D)
Beautiful dog.

MARCUS
His name is Anchor. A rescue. Five years now.

ELENA
No family nearby? Children?

MARCUS
(flat)
No. No children. It is just Anchor and me.

He pours the tea and sets it on the table.

title: 4、INT. LIGHTHOUSE - UPPER FLOOR - LATE AFTERNOON.
content:
INT. LIGHTHOUSE - UPPER FLOOR - LATE AFTERNOON

Marcus leads Elena up the iron spiral staircase. At the top landing, below the lantern room, a narrow corridor has two doors. One stands open -- a storage room crowded with old equipment. The other door is CLOSED and secured with a heavy padlock.

Elena pauses.

ELENA
What's in the locked one?

MARCUS
(not stopping)
Old coast guard material. Nothing that concerns your story.

ELENA
Could I--

MARCUS
No.

He continues up toward the lantern. Elena lingers at the locked door, studying it. Then she descends to the entrance hall.

INT. MAIN ENTRANCE HALL - CONTINUOUS

Elena pauses at the base of the staircase. There, mounted on the wall right beside the MAIN ENTRANCE DOOR, hangs a SILVER KEY on a simple iron hook. Small. Old. It catches the afternoon light.

She photographs it with her phone and opens her green spiral notebook.

ELENA
(writing quietly)
Silver key. Hook beside the main door.

She caps the pen and slips the notebook back into her pocket.

title: 5、INT. DEPUTY'S OFFICE - DAY.
content:
INT. DEPUTY'S OFFICE - DAY

A small-town law satellite office. Bulletin board covered in notices, a cluttered desk. TOM BRIGGS (40s, stocky, unhurried) leans back in his chair and regards Elena across the desk.

ELENA
Deputy Briggs -- how long has Marcus been out at the lighthouse?

TOM
Twenty years. He came when old Gareth retired. Former merchant marine, Marcus. Quiet man. No trouble ever.

ELENA
(writing in her green notebook)
And the station itself -- how far back does it go?

Tom swivels and pulls a laminated fact sheet from his bulletin board.

TOM
Built in 1887. One of the original iron-frame coastal towers on this stretch. Still functioning under civilian contract since the eighties.

ELENA
There's a locked room on the upper floor. You know anything about that?

Tom goes still.

TOM
Can't say I do.

ELENA
Sure.

TOM
(leaning forward)
Ms. Voss. Marcus is a private man. Twenty years alone out there -- people form habits. That's his business.

Elena stands and extends a hand.

ELENA
Thank you, Deputy Briggs.

title: 6、INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S QUARTERS - EVENING.
content:
INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S QUARTERS - EVENING

Elena returns to find Marcus at the kitchen table, papers spread before him. From outside, a dog barks.

MARCUS
(calling through the door)
Captain! Easy!

The barking stops. Marcus glances at Elena.

MARCUS (CONT'D)
He gets wound up when the pressure drops.

Elena sets her bag down.

ELENA
Your leg. Is it an old injury?

MARCUS
Left leg. Fishing trawler, 1991. A cable snapped. Lucky I kept it.

ELENA
The stairs must be hard.

MARCUS
You manage.

A pause. Elena glances toward the window.

ELENA
I came back a different route this evening. There was a vehicle near the outbuilding when I pulled in.

MARCUS
That's Tom Briggs's. Borrowed it -- my own vehicle is in for service.

ELENA
So you saw me drive in with the blue one?

MARCUS
(nodding)
Hard to miss on this road. Only vehicle that came up all evening.

Elena opens her notebook and writes something she underlines twice.

title: 7、INT. LIGHTHOUSE - WATCH ROOM - MORNING.
content:
INT. LIGHTHOUSE - WATCH ROOM - MORNING

Early light fills the watch room. Elena sits across from Marcus, a YELLOW LEGAL PAD open on her knee. She taps her pen.

Marcus sets a large BLACK LOGBOOK on the desk between them.

MARCUS
This covers 1910 to 1940. Most of what you would find useful is in here.

Elena pages through it, making notes on her yellow legal pad.

ELENA
People in town mentioned you. One said you'd been out here as long as anyone could remember.

MARCUS
Long enough.

ELENA
Thirty years, they said.

MARCUS
Give or take.

Elena's phone buzzes. She steps back slightly and answers it.

ELENA
(into phone)
Diane, yes. I'm still with him. I'll have the draft by Friday, I promise.

She hangs up. Marcus has moved to the window. Elena offers him a cup of coffee poured from a thermos.

ELENA (CONT'D)
Coffee?

MARCUS
(firm shake of his head)
No. I've never taken to hot drinks. Never have. You go ahead.

She pours a cup and studies him over the rim.

title: 8、INT. LIGHTHOUSE - NIGHT.
content:
INT. LIGHTHOUSE - WATCH ROOM - NIGHT

Late. The watch room lit by a single lamp. Elena is still working when Marcus appears at the top of the stairs.

MARCUS
You should sleep. There's a cot in the equipment room.

ELENA
Just finishing. Your wife -- you must miss her. Ten years is a long time to be alone out here.

MARCUS
(quietly)
You learn to manage it.

ELENA
Does your daughter ever come to visit?

A pause.

MARCUS
She comes when she can. Long drive.

ELENA
What's her name?

MARCUS
Rose.

Elena writes.

ELENA
The locked room. I'd really like to understand what's in there.

MARCUS
It is not part of your story.

ELENA
With respect, I think it might be.

A long pause. Marcus crosses the room and reaches above the window sill beside the main instrument panel, retrieving a small KEY on a cord. It is BRASS. Worn smooth.

MARCUS
All right. Come.

He leads her not upward but DOWN -- a staircase she has not noticed before, descending below the main floor to a heavy door at the bottom.

ELENA
(surprised)
I thought the locked room was upstairs.

MARCUS
That's just storage. This is what you came here for.

title: 9、EXT. HARBOR - DAY.
content:
EXT. HARBOR - DAY

Elena finds TOM on the dock, watching a fishing vessel unload.

ELENA
Chief Briggs. I wanted to follow up.

TOM
Chief's generous. What's on your mind?

ELENA
The lighthouse. Can you confirm when it was built?

TOM
(leaning on a post)
1923, wasn't it. Part of the coastal modernization program. Six towers built that year along this stretch.

Elena writes carefully.

ELENA
And Marcus -- personally?

TOM
Good man. Sharp. Never needed glasses a day in his life, from what I know. Can still read the tide charts from across the room without squinting.

Elena's pen slows.

ELENA
Right.

A GOLDEN RETRIEVER comes bounding down the dock, circling Tom's legs.

TOM
That's Anchor. Marcus must have walked him down this morning.

Marcus appears at the far end of the dock, the golden retriever leaping at his hands.

MARCUS
(calling over)
Ms. Voss. Finished?

Elena watches the golden retriever and adds a note to her yellow legal pad.

FADE OUT.

END OF STORY.
